pamphlet_excerpts: Hand Blister Risks: In rowing, blisters are most likely to occur on the hands (p. 13).
Early Blister Warning Signs: Pay attention to any tender or sensitive areas (hot spots) that indicate the start of a blister (p. 13).
Grip Friction Adjustment: You may be able to adjust or relax your grip to avoid friction on the sensitive area (p. 13).
Protective Rowing Gloves: If you are prone to blisters, prevent them by wearing rowing gloves (p. 13).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Relax Your Oar Grip: You may be able to adjust or relax your grip to avoid friction on the sensitive area (p. 13).
Step 2 - Wear Protective Rowing Gloves: If you are prone to blisters, prevent them by wearing rowing gloves (p. 13).
Step 3 - Cover and Protect Blisters: If you do get a blister, cover and protect the area from further irritation (p. 13).

Step 4 - Identify Overstretched Joint Ligaments: A sprain occurs when an ankle, wrist, or other joint is bent far enough to over stretch the ligaments, the tough bands that hold joints together (p. 13).

options: A. Row standing up facing the bow, and swim for the nearest shore immediately if the rowboat swamps in cold water.
B. Rely entirely on sound to detect other boats ahead, and overturn a swamped rowboat so air escapes from under the thwarts.

Roll Onto Boat Bottom: Then roll over so that you fall into the bottom of the swamped boat, landing on your backside (p. 65).
Counterbalancing Your Partner: You can then lean over the side to counterbalance as your friend follows the same steps to come in over the opposite side (p. 65).

Step 3 - Press the Gunwale: Remember that when you pull yourself up on the gunwale, the gunwale will be forced down into the water (p. 65).
Step 4 - Shift Weight Off Gunwale: After you roll in and get your weight off the gunwale, it will rise back (p. 65).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which statement accurately compares common rowboat hull materials?
quiz_item.question: Which statement accurately compares common rowboat hull materials?
options: A. Aluminum is naturally buoyant and floats without any internal air or foam chambers.
B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.
C. Wood planking sinks immediately when swamped unless fitted with metal air tanks.
D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
choices: A. Aluminum is naturally buoyant and floats without any internal air or foam chambers.
B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.
C. Wood planking sinks immediately when swamped unless fitted with metal air tanks.
D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Wood planking is easy to cut and drill and has natural buoyancy that keeps a wooden rowboat afloat even when filled with water, whereas aluminum requires built-in flotation chambers (p. 25).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: From which direction should you always make your final approach to a swimmer in the water?
quiz_item.question: From which direction should you always make your final approach to a swimmer in the water?
options: A. Into the wind or against the current to maintain precise control of the boat.
B. Downwind with the waves pushing the stern at maximum speed.
C. Broadside to the wind and waves so the boat drifts sideways into the swimmer.
D. With both oars shipped inside the boat while coasting with the current.
choices: A. Into the wind or against the current to maintain precise control of the boat.
B. Downwind with the waves pushing the stern at maximum speed.
C. Broadside to the wind and waves so the boat drifts sideways into the swimmer.
D. With both oars shipped inside the boat while coasting with the current.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Into the wind or against the current to maintain precise control of the boat.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Approaching a swimmer into the wind or against the current gives the rower much better control over speed and alignment when stopping at the person in the water (p. 67).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Because a rower in a fixed-seat rowboat faces the stern while propelling the boat bow-first, how should you navigate safely and handle a swamped boat if it fills with water?
options: A. Row standing up facing the bow, and swim for the nearest shore immediately if the rowboat swamps in cold water.
B. Rely entirely on sound to detect other boats ahead, and overturn a swamped rowboat so air escapes from under the thwarts.
C. Tie your ankles to the floorboards for leverage, and remove your USCG lifejacket if water enters the hull.

D. Look over your shoulder every few strokes (or use a stern lookout) to check your course ahead, wear a USCG-approved PFD, and stay with a swamped rowboat because its built-in flotation will support you.
choices: A. Row standing up facing the bow, and swim for the nearest shore immediately if the rowboat swamps in cold water.
B. Rely entirely on sound to detect other boats ahead, and overturn a swamped rowboat so air escapes from under the thwarts.
C. Tie your ankles to the floorboards for leverage, and remove your USCG lifejacket if water enters the hull.

D. Look over your shoulder every few strokes (or use a stern lookout) to check your course ahead, wear a USCG-approved PFD, and stay with a swamped rowboat because its built-in flotation will support you.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Look over your shoulder every few strokes (or use a stern lookout) to check your course ahead, wear a USCG-approved PFD, and stay with a swamped rowboat because its built-in flotation will support you.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Rowers face backward and must glance over their shoulder every few strokes to watch for hazards, always wear a USCG-approved PFD under Safety Afloat, and stay with a swamped boat rather than swimming far to shore.

choices: A. Pass the beginner swim test and carry a whistle on a lanyard.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Pass the Scouting America swimmer test and have a buddy with you or nearby in another boat.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Safety Afloat and the Rowing merit badge require all rowers to pass the Scouting America swimmer test and always have a buddy in the same boat or nearby in another boat (p. 15).

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Rowing shells, sculling craft, and canoes with drop-in units should be removed from the water after use and stored upside down on well-supported racks protected from sun, wind, and water (p. 40).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the correct procedure if your canoe rowing rig or rowboat capsizes and swamps in deep water?
options: A. Abandon the boat immediately and swim toward the nearest shoreline.
B. Stay with the craft, reenter over the gunwale, sit flat on the bottom, and paddle to shore with one oar.
C. Stand upright on the center thwart and wave both oars overhead until help arrives.
D. Dive underneath the hull to untie the foot stretchers before swimming away.
choices: A. Abandon the boat immediately and swim toward the nearest shoreline.
B. Stay with the craft, reenter over the gunwale, sit flat on the bottom, and paddle to shore with one oar.
C. Stand upright on the center thwart and wave both oars overhead until help arrives.
D. Dive underneath the hull to untie the foot stretchers before swimming away.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Stay with the craft, reenter over the gunwale, sit flat on the bottom, and paddle to shore with one oar.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): If your craft swamps, you should stay with the boat, reenter over the gunwale using the flop-over method, sit flat on the bottom for stability, and paddle to shore with one oar (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you position your rowboat to rescue and tow a tired swimmer 20 yards from shore?
options: A. Row at full speed bow-first and tell the swimmer to grab the moving oar blades.
B. Throw both oars into the water and dive overboard to push the swimmer ashore.
C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
D. Have the swimmer climb over the narrow bow deck while you stand in the stern.
choices: A. Row at full speed bow-first and tell the swimmer to grab the moving oar blades.
B. Throw both oars into the water and dive overboard to push the swimmer ashore.
C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
D. Have the swimmer climb over the narrow bow deck while you stand in the stern.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In a rowboat swimmer rescue, you row out to the swimmer, pivot the boat, and back the stern within reach while giving clear instructions so they can hold the transom for a tow to shore (p. 79).

B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.
C. Wood planking sinks immediately when swamped unless fitted with metal air tanks.
D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
choices: A. Aluminum is naturally buoyant and floats without any internal air or foam chambers.
B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Wood planking is easy to cut and drill and has natural buoyancy that keeps a wooden rowboat afloat even when filled with water, whereas aluminum requires built-in flotation chambers (p. 25).
